findings.asked: Work done pulling a box, define power, then find a time from power and work.
findings.wentWrong: Only a minority recalled work = force x distance; the definition of power was explained as energy, force or strength; the time calculation went better.
findings.rule: Power is the rate of doing work - work done (or energy transferred) per second.

findings.asked: The same box-up-a-slope question at Higher.
findings.wentWrong: Work done was right (500 J), but the power definition was the hardest part of the whole paper: candidates knew it involved energy or work and time but did not link them as a rate.
findings.rule: Definition = work done divided by time taken; say 'per second' or 'rate'.

findings.asked: Work done by a forklift lifting a load, then the time taken at a given power.
findings.wentWrong: The method was known but many kept the distance in centimetres and lost two of the four marks.
findings.rule: Distance in metres before you multiply.

ruleToRemember: Work done = force x distance moved in the direction of the force (J, with distance in m). Power = work done (or energy transferred) divided by time - the rate of doing work, in watts. Definitions need the 'per unit time' idea, not just the words energy and time.
aStarSignal: Defining power as a rate in one sentence and using P = W/t to find a time, with units converted first.
